title: Automate one small thing well
description: Choose a sensible first automation and test triggers, approvals, failures, and recovery.

sections.title: Choose a repeatable, low-stakes task
sections.body: Look for work with a clear input, stable rules, and an output you can verify. Standard software rules may be enough; not every automation needs an AI model. Use AI when the task benefits from language interpretation or flexible classification, and keep the scope small while you learn.
bullets: Estimate current effort and common mistakes.
Avoid starting with payments, deletion, or irreversible commitments.

sections.title: Map the workflow before connecting tools
sections.body: Write the trigger, input, transformation, review, and output. Check which accounts and permissions are needed. Decide where a person approves the result. Give the workflow only the access it requires, and protect any credentials through the platform’s supported secret settings.
bullets: Make repeated events safe to handle.
Set limits on volume, runtime, and spending.

sections.title: Test failure and recovery
sections.body: Try missing fields, duplicate inputs, unavailable services, and incorrect classifications. Define what happens when a step fails. Keep a log that helps you investigate without exposing sensitive information. Run a pilot alongside the manual process and compare quality before depending on the automation.
bullets: Build a visible stop or disable option.
Record how to recover work that only partly completed.

example.title: A good first pilot
example.text: A form submission creates a draft internal task with a suggested category. A team member checks the category before assignment. Duplicate submissions are recognized so the workflow does not create repeated tasks.

exercise: Map one routine task in five boxes. Mark which steps need rules, AI assistance, or human review, and write one failure case for each.

faq.question: Do I need coding skills?
faq.answer: Many automation tools provide visual builders. You still need to understand permissions, logic, errors, and the consequences of each action.

faq.question: How do I know automation saved time?
faq.answer: Compare total effort, including setup, corrections, monitoring, and failures, against the previous process.

sources.name: OWASP: Top risks for generative AI applications
